ans.q: I love optical illusion art and pareidolia, any good websites or blogs that explain how our brains see faces in random things?
names: why do we see faces in objects
ans.snip:
Absolutely — if you’re into optical illusion art and pareidolia, there are some great science-friendly sites that explain why our brains keep “finding” faces in clouds, rocks, outlets, toast, and random patterns.

Here are some solid places to start:

1. Scientific American
Website: https://www.scientificamerican.com  
Search their site for pareidolia or face recognition. They often publish accessible articles about why the brain is wired to detect faces so quickly.

2. The Conversation
Website: https://theconversation.com  
This is a great source for readable articles by researchers. Search for “pareidolia,” “face detection,” or “visual perception.” They usually explain the neuroscience clearly without being too technical.

3. Psychology Today
Website: https://www.psychologytoday.com  
They have articles on pattern recognition, illusion perception, and why humans are so face-sensitive.
